character.description: The exact currently accepted body-only SwordReady v002 frame0 identity, fixed native right three-quarter view; common bare grey/charcoal cloth body and original brown gloves/boots

death.action: Fixed native RIGHT-facing three-quarter camera from the attached accepted SwordReady v002 frame0. The row owns motion only. Bare charcoal/grey cloth shirt and trousers, original belt, brown gloves and boots; rigid squat crooked bell/clock helmet, original knob and face opening with two contained amber eyes. Preserve the accepted anchor's actual shapes, proportions, palette and hand-ink weight. Same common drawing scale through the complete row: 416-source-pixel standing-equivalent body is a design target on 512 cells, not a demand that crouched/lying bboxes be 416 high. Never normalize, lengthen limbs, stretch the helmet or enlarge a small pose. The future weapon and armor are modular; paint only genuine connected body/glove/boot pixels. No sword/handle/rod/shield/staff/crossbow, no chest or shoulder armor, bracer or shin plate. Hands must be genuinely drawn with connected short upper arm, elbow, forearm, wrist and believable thumb/fingers. Near/far arms stay distinct; no fixed copied grip coordinate, no invented identical socket, no technical dots/axes. Near glove may naturally close around an invisible later handle, but never force it to an old socket or copy an old hand. Actual grip/axis, body contacts, crown and module occlusion are unknown until generated pixels are measured. Native actor translation is external; do not draw floor, trails, shadows, displaced duplicates, dust, glow or speed effects. Do not attach old v006 body art, canonical131 original sheet or any alternate identity. A nonloop articulated collapse, not a rotated standing cutout. The final fifth corpse starts at .80 seconds and holds until state changes. There is no .80 gameplay death deadline. Keep a natural near hand suitable for a later measured retained-weapon grip; do not paint a dropped weapon or imply an inventory drop. Corpse orientation is body pose only and never moves the actor root. Exact ordered pose progression: Pose 0: Immediate loss of strength: visibly distinct slack shoulders and bent knees; recognizable rigid clock helmet remains attached. Pose 1: Knees buckle and torso drops: hips rotate, both boots and hand/wrist configuration change; no whole-body image rotation. Pose 2: Body falls with real articulated anatomy: torso and thighs rotate relative to each other, helmet remains rigid, hands/forearms are not detached. Pose 3: Ground impact and settling: authentic supported body contact, limbs finish folding, helmet and boots fit wholly within the same source cell. Pose 4: Stable recognizable corpse: relaxed supported silhouette, true final separate hand/wrist and helmet contours; remains the terminal pose indefinitely.
